season: In Tamil Nadu paddy is grown in Kuruvai (June–September), Samba (August–January), Thaladi and Navarai seasons.
soil: Clay or clay-loam soils that hold water suit paddy.

season: Tomato is commonly transplanted in June–July, November–December and January–February.
duration: about 60–75 days from transplanting to first harvest
soil: Well-drained loam rich in organic matter, pH about 6–7.

season: Chilli is commonly transplanted in January–February, June–July and September–October.
duration: about 75 days from transplanting to first green chilli harvest
soil: Well-drained loam; chilli is sensitive to waterlogging.

season: Banana is commonly planted in February–April, and with the monsoon in some districts.
Coconut seedlings are best planted at the start of the monsoon (June–July or September–October).
duration: about 6–7 years to bearing for tall varieties and 3–4 years for hybrid/dwarf varieties
soil: Well-drained red loam, sandy loam or coastal sandy soils.

season: Sugarcane is planted in the early season (December–January), mid season (February–March) and late season (April–May).
soil: Deep loam or clay-loam with good drainage.

season: Groundnut is sown in June–July (rainfed) and December–January (irrigated).
soil: Well-drained light soils such as red sandy loam that allow easy pegging.

season: Cotton is sown in August–September (winter irrigated) and February–March (summer irrigated).
soil: Deep black soils or well-drained loams.

season: Maize is sown in June–July, September–October and January–February.
soil: Well-drained loam; maize does not tolerate waterlogging.

season: Brinjal is commonly transplanted in December–January and May–June.
duration: about 55–65 days from transplanting to first harvest
soil: Well-drained loam rich in organic matter.

season: Small onion is commonly planted in April–May and October–November; timing varies by district.
Annual drumstick varieties such as PKM-1 are commonly sown in June–July.
duration: first pods in about 6 months for annual varieties
soil: Well-drained sandy loam; tolerates poor soils but not waterlogging.

season: Black gram is sown in June–July and September–October, and as a rice-fallow crop in January in the delta.
soil: Well-drained loam; also grown on residual moisture in rice fallows.

season: Green gram is sown in June–July and September–October, and as a rice-fallow crop in the delta.
soil: Well-drained loam; also grown on residual moisture in rice fallows.
